clue.text: Smart not to end up like Katharina

definitions.note: Katharina is the title character tamed in Shakespeare's comedy, the best-known example of the type

indicators.note: not ending means the synonym for smart stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: smart means shrewd, clever in practical matters

explanation.surface: A warning to be clever enough not to finish as Shakespeare's bad-tempered heroine did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to end up' drops the final D of SHREWD. Katharina is the scold of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, so 'like' leads to her as the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Katharina is the scolding woman tamed by Petruchio in Shakespeare's play.

definitions.note: Mother Shipton was a legendary Yorkshire prophetess and reputed witch

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the preceding letters might be something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ill-tempered prophet, possibly the legendary Yorkshire fortune-teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the only anagram signal, rearranging CROSS SEER. Mother Shipton was a 16th-century Yorkshire prophetess reputed to be a witch, so she is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Mother Shipton, the Yorkshire prophetess, was reputed to be a witch with magic powers.

indicators.note: failure suggests the word heart has broken down, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cardiac arrest that came too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failure' rearranges HEART. The answer is an old poetic word, as in Milton's 'rathe primrose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic poetic synonym: it describes something blooming or ripening before the usual time.

definitions.meaning: attending on diners at table, bringing their food
a delaying tactic, holding back until the moment favours you, is called this kind of game

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is attending at table; the other names the game of patient delay played by someone biding their time.

parts.note: watertight is read as two words, water being tight or scarce: in a drought the mains are cut and people draw water from a tap set up in the street

explanation.surface: A tap that is only turned on once it has stopped leaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks you to hear 'watertight' as 'water tight', water being in short supply. In British droughts, upright street taps are set up for households to share.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an upright street tap is what households queue at when supplies are rationed.

definitions.meaning: the name of a London gentlemen's club for people in the arts, founded in 1857
an old term for an uncivilised or brutal person

explanation.surface: A cudgel suited to a caveman.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a London arts society and is also an old noun for a brutal, uncivilised person.

definitions.meaning: the Hawker Hurricane was a British fighter plane of the Second World War
whimsically, the study of the atmosphere could be called the skill or trade of the skies

explanation.definitionFit: The Hawker fighter plane is an example; whimsically split in two, the word describes skill with the atmosphere.

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters in the word before it

explanation.surface: The purpose of altering a patient's treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges MEDICAL. 'Point' looks like purpose, but it is the dot in a number such as 3.14.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand: the dot separating whole numbers from fractions is often called simply this.

clue.text: One who thinks little of other people

definitions.text: One who thinks little of other people

parts.words: One who thinks little of other people
parts.note: not someone scornful of others, but someone whose thoughts turn inward to the self rather than outward to company

explanation.surface: Someone with a low opinion of everybody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thinks little of' usually means despises; here it is literal, spending little thought on others because attention is turned inward.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: such a person's attention is directed inward on their own mind.

parts.note: brood is a noun, the young of a bird of prey, and the high places are the crags where the nest is built

explanation.surface: Someone sulking at the top of the organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brood' reads as a verb for sulking, but it is the noun for a bird's young: an eagle's nest on a crag, a word also used for the young in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: an eagle's nest on a crag, and also the young raised in it.

clue.text: One who gets his own back — the dog

definitions.text: One who gets his own back
definitions.meaning: read literally, a person who recovers what belongs to him
a breed of gundog trained to fetch shot game

explanation.surface: A man takes his revenge, the scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering property does this literally, and the gundog breed is named for fetching game.

clue.text: Provide the king with choice food first

indicators.note: first says the choice food is placed ahead of the king in the answer

parts.note: a cate is an old word for a delicacy or dainty
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Serve His Majesty the finest dishes before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts CATE before R. Cate, usually met in the plural, is an archaic word for a delicacy; R is rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to supply what is needed, especially meals for an event.

clue.text: Never promise gin is obtainable — this doesn't open till late

indicators.note: is obtainable says the answer can be got out of these letters by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Don't guarantee spirits at a bar that keeps late hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is obtainable' rearranges NEVER PROMISE GIN. The definition sounds like a pub or shop but describes a flower whose blooms unfold at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: this plant's yellow flowers unfold at dusk.

definitions.meaning: to hire someone, or to join battle with an opponent
to employ or book someone to do a piece of work

explanation.definitionFit: Both are synonyms for hiring: you book a person's services for a job.

clue.text: Winchester athlete — one who moves his arms about

definitions.text: one who moves his arms about

parts.note: a Winchester is a make of repeating rifle, an example of a gun
a runner is one kind of athlete

explanation.surface: A sportsman from the English cathedral city who flails his limbs as he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester looks like the English city or its school; it is the rifle. The 'arms' are weapons, moved about illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a smuggler who transports weapons from place to place.

parts.note: F is the music abbreviation for forte, loud
glib means fluent, speaking smoothly and easily

explanation.surface: A noisy, smooth-talking set of fashionable people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to J. K. Galbraith's 1958 phrase for a wealthy consumer society.
explanation.definitionFit: Collocation: Galbraith's famous phrase describes a wealthy, prosperous society.

clue.text: It shows the holder of the championship record

parts.note: a title is a championship, as in winning the league title
a deed is a written legal record of an agreement

explanation.surface: A document naming whoever currently has the sporting record.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all sport, but the holder is the owner of a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the legal document proving who owns a property.

parts.note: a scot was a historical tax or levy, as in scot-free, so taxes are scots
a hand is a man, a worker, as in all hands on deck

explanation.surface: The country burdens its experienced worker with levies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' reads as an adjective and 'taxes' as a verb; both are nouns here. A scot was an old levy, surviving in 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a citizen of one of the UK's nations, the one north of England.

clue.text: Meaningful words spoken by the judge

definitions.text: Meaningful words spoken by the judge

parts.words: Meaningful words spoken by the judge
parts.note: two senses meet: a grammatical unit of words that makes sense, and the punishment a judge pronounces in court

explanation.surface: A judge makes a weighty remark in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue fuses two senses: a set of words making complete sense, and the punishment a judge pronounces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a grammatical unit that makes sense and the punishment pronounced in court.

clue.text: Provided for a tip, being in debted.

parts.note: the tip of something is its end
being indebted is having owed money

explanation.surface: Leaving a gratuity because one feels under an obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip is an extremity, not a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: given a permanent income or fund, as a college or hospital may be.

clue.text: Group hold note in musical composition

indicators.note: hold says the group has the note inside it

parts.note: a sept is a clan or branch of a family, especially in Ireland or Scotland
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An ensemble sustains one pitch during a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' wants to be the definition, since the answer is also a band of seven; it is the clan, and 'hold' makes it the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a piece written for seven performers.

clue.text: Dominate bridge players and save about a pound

parts.note: East and North are two of the four seats at the bridge table

indicators.note: about says the word save goes round the pound

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Beat everyone at the card table and come out roughly a quid ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps SAVE round L, the old abbreviation for a pound, after two bridge seats, East and North.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bring someone completely under your control.

parts.note: to count is to calculate a total
Y is a letter used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Work out the missing value in the equation by dividing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all arithmetic, but the division is a region of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an administrative region of Britain or Ireland, such as Kent or Cork.

clue.text: College rock formation in place for opening ceremony

definitions.text: formation in place for opening ceremony

parts.note: a foundation is an endowed institution such as a college or hospital
a rock is a stone

explanation.surface: A university band lines up ready for the inaugural festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: A college is a foundation in the sense of an endowed institution. The ceremony is the formal laying of a building's first block.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the block ceremonially laid to mark the start of a new building.

definitions.meaning: printed documents with blank spaces for you to complete

explanation.surface: Outlines waiting to be coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both outlines and the official papers with blanks you complete.

parts.note: or is the word that introduces an alternative
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Another option besides the army headquarters in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German' is a request for the word 'the' in German, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an instruction that must be obeyed.

parts.note: René is a man's name
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogy

explanation.surface: A married couple make a fresh beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to resume something after a break.

clue.text: Chap with a title has pull

parts.note: a chap is a man
handle is slang for a name or title, as in a handle to one's name

explanation.surface: A fellow with a knighthood enjoys influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pull' reads as influence; it is the physical act of hauling something about. A handle is slang for a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: to haul or shove something roughly by physical effort.

clue.text: Noisiness of many in New York after street parade

indicators.note: after says the many in New York follow the street and parade in the answer

parts.note: a ride can be a mounted procession, a kind of parade

indicators.note: in places the many inside the letters for New York

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, loosely many

explanation.surface: The din of crowds in Manhattan following a procession down the avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'after' set the order. 'many' is the crossword habit of using a large Roman numeral, here a hundred, for an unspecified crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the quality of being harsh, loud and grating.

definitions.meaning: bearing spikes of grain, as ripening corn does
one family of seals, including sea lions, has visible outer flaps for hearing

explanation.surface: Bristling with spines as a sea mammal might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn in spike is described this way, and one seal family is named for its visible outer flaps.
